posts.headline: Bitcoin has slipped to a four-month low — and the people who bought it this fall are now about 20% underwater.
posts.caption:
Bitcoin just hit its lowest level since the summer — and recent buyers are feeling it most.

It traded around $64,000 Wednesday morning, after dipping near $61,000 on Nov. 15, a four-month low (CoinDesk). That's about 20% below what people who bought in the last one to three months paid for it.

Why it's your money, not just a trader's: crypto has crept into everyday savings — spot Bitcoin ETFs and some retirement menus, in the US and Canada alike. A 20% drop there is real money.

My take: if crypto sits in your long-term savings, size it so a slide like this is survivable — the people hurting most bought recently and bought big.

How much of your savings, if any, is in crypto?

#Bitcoin #Crypto #Investing #Retirement

Source: CoinDesk market coverage, Nov. 18, 2026
Educational only — not financial advice.
